name: United States Postal Service

profile.address: 900, North Alameda Street, New Chinatown, Civic Center, Chinatown, Los Angeles, Los Angeles County, California, 90012
profile.reading:
The Terminal Annex is a large historic post office building at 900 North Alameda Street in downtown Los Angeles, next to Union Station and the city's Chinatown and Civic Center districts. Built between 1938 and 1940, it is recognized as a California Historical Landmark and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places for its architecture and its role in the city's mail handling history during the mid twentieth century, when Los Angeles grew into one of the country's major postal hubs.

The building is owned and operated by the United States Postal Service, an independent federal agency, and its primary documented function remains postal. Mail processing and related USPS operations tied to its historic role as a rail adjacent terminal facility are what the public record actually describes. Some equipment and engineering references associated with the building point to IT and network infrastructure being housed within it alongside its postal functions, which would be consistent with USPS's general practice of folding data and network equipment into its existing nationwide real estate footprint rather than building purpose made data center campuses for every regional need. That practice does not make the Terminal Annex primarily a data center, however, and no USPS publication, capacity disclosure, or independent source describes this site as a dedicated data center facility with its own power, cooling, or tenancy profile. Its public identity, landmark status, and available documentation all center on its postal and historic architectural significance rather than any computing infrastructure it may also contain.

profile.research_note:
[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is the Los Angeles Terminal Annex, a large historic post office building at 900 North Alameda Street in downtown Los Angeles, built between 1938 and 1940 and listed as a California Historical Landmark and on the National Register of Historic Places, operated by the United States Postal Service, an independent federal agency. Engineering documentation from DCM Designs, a firm whose project listings reference a data center built at the Terminal Annex, indicates the historic building houses IT infrastructure in addition to its original mail processing and postal functions, consistent with USPS practice of maintaining regional data and network operations within its existing real estate footprint. USPS operates its own nationwide IT infrastructure supporting mail tracking, logistics, retail, and administrative systems, and the Terminal Annex facility is plausibly one node in that network given its downtown Los Angeles location and postal history, but no USPS owned publication describing the Terminal Annex data center capacity, function, or current operational status in detail was found. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

[pass 2026-09-04] Confirmed via public landmark and postal record research that the Terminal Annex primary documented function is postal operations and historic preservation, not a dedicated data center. No independent source describes this site as a purpose built or primary data center facility, so reading was shortened below 350 words and specs_unpublished set to true per house rules for buildings that are likely not primarily data centers.
